derivedFrom: the captured constituents payload read through the rules in section 7, not from a run. The spans come from HistoricalTickerComponents, which is where the provider puts dates; Components is tonight's snapshot and holds none. Widened to four names at 3.6: the payload was recaptured and re-trimmed rather than having a row spliced into the earlier one, so every row here came from one payload.
note: constituents and names are different populations: a constituent is a membership row and a name is a ticker with a captured price series, so the two departed constituents are owed no series.
sectorNote: derived from the Components object of the same captured payload, which is where the provider puts Sector and carries current members alone. The two departed constituents appear in the spans and not in Components, so their sector is null, which is what the provider says rather than an omission.
industryNote: derived from the same Components object as the sectors, from 6.9, where the industry became what a theme is. Four members and four industries, so no two of this fixture's names share a theme, and the claim that one theme pass serves every member of an industry is asserted over a constructed pair rather than over these four. The departed constituents have no industry for the reason they have no sector.
nameNote: derived from the HistoricalTickerComponents object of the same captured payload, which states a Name on every span, the two departed constituents included, where Components carries current members alone. Read off the payload by hand, not from a run.
